title: Distinctness conjecture for coprime values of the divisor-sum ratio
statement:
Let $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$ be coprime and satisfy $x\ne y$. **Distinctness conjecture.** The values

$$
\frac{\sigma(x)}{x}\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{\sigma(y)}{y}
$$

are distinct. Here $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function. Distinctness is known for squarefree inputs, but the conjecture remains open for arbitrary distinct coprime natural numbers and is related to the odd $k$-perfect number conjecture.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15628

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).
source_name: Mario Ziller, “Orders and partitions of integers induced by arithmetic functions”, arXiv:2310.15628 (2026).
